text:
linda: Customer on prod reporting SSE stream cuts out after ~90s, sometimes with a 401 mid-stream. App is iOS, behind corp proxy. Need cURL repro + request IDs and any headers we can inspect.

devraj: Can you grab the request id(s) from the response headers? Also ask them to run a simple curl that dumps headers (-D -) so we can see X-Request-Id and auth. Proxy details would help too.

linda: From their logs: 
```
X-Request-Id: req_01GABCDEF
X-Trace-Id: trace_0xabc123
Status: 200 -> then 401 after ~90s
```
They're using cookie auth (Set-Cookie session=...). Partial curl they used: 
```
curl -v "https://api.redwood.internal/v1/stream?model=text-embed" \ 
  -H "Cookie: session=abcd1234" \ 
  --compressed -N
```

ajohnson: Cookie-based auth + token rotation is a common culprit. If the session token is short-lived and the client reconnects or re-requests headers aren't sent on follow-ups, we'll see mid-stream 401. Ask them to try header-based Bearer token for repro. Also capture response headers and raw stream.

linda: Asking them to run this exact command and paste the output (keep output short):
```
# dump headers and stream body, no buffering for immediate output
curl -v -D - -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Connection: keep-alive" \ 
  -N --no-buffer "https://api.redwood.internal/v1/stream?model=gpt-lite&stream=1" \ 
  --trace-ascii ./curl_trace.txt
```
Notes: -D - prints response headers to stdout, -N/--no-buffer keeps streaming output immediate, --trace-ascii records TCP-level traces to inspect proxy handshake.

maria: If they're behind a corporate proxy, include `--proxy http://proxy.company:8080`. Also if the proxy does HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 translation we recommend forcing HTTP/1.1 for repro with `--http1.1`.

devraj: Add `-H "Expect:"` if curl is sending an `Expect: 100-continue` header. Some proxies behave oddly. Also confirm they aren't using `Connection: close` anywhere.

support-bot: Debug-bundle request received. To the customer: please run the above curl, attach `curl_trace.txt` and the raw output, and we'll trigger a debug collection. Use the trace id: `trace_0xabc123` and request id: `req_01GABCDEF` when uploading.

linda: Customer pasted output excerpt: 
```
> GET /v1/stream?model=gpt-lite&stream=1 HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< X-Request-Id: req_01GABCDEF
< X-Trace-Id: trace_0xabc123
... (streamed chunks) ...
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< X-Request-Id: req_01GABCDEF
```
They also attached `curl_trace.txt` showing a small burst of rehandshake around t+88s. Uploaded debug bundle to s3://redwood-debug/trace_0xabc123-1767777777.zip (internal only).

ajohnson: That pattern lines up with token rotation at ~60-90s. For a short-term repro ask them to: (1) use header Bearer token that does not rotate, (2) force http1.1, (3) include -D - and --trace-ascii so we can see proxy CONNECT/keepalive. If that stops the 401 mid-stream, it's definitely auth refresh.

devraj: For validation steps we usually ask for two runs: one with cookie auth (their current) and one with stable Bearer header. Please also include `-i` or `-D -` so we capture response headers for every HTTP response chunk.

linda: I'll send the exact commands and ask them to run both variants + upload traces. Closing loop for now, will follow up when they give outputs. Thanks :pray:

maria: Quick tip: if they can't switch tokens easily, a test using a long-lived service key does the trick for debugging; do not share keys in public channels.

linda: customer will test and we have the debug bundle. Marking this thread as awaiting-customer. :white_check_mark:
